stem:
Damini wants to expand $(z+9)(z-9)$ by recognising a conjugate pair.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: $(z+9)(z-9)=z^{2}+81$, keeping both signs as addition in the product.
The expanded difference $z^{2}-81$ is what creates the factors $(z+9)$ and $(z-9)$.
$(z+9)(z-9)=z^{2}-81$, because the factors share the same terms with opposite signs.
$(z+9)(z-9)=z^{2}+18z-81$, as if both middle terms stay after expansion.

teacher.key_rationale: Conjugate factors (z+9)(z-9) expand to z²−81 with cross-terms cancelling. Dropping the opposite-sign condition yields z²+81. Saying the difference creates the factors reverses the recognition direction. Keeping a middle ±18z uses a different expansion identity.
